root_cause: Rendered rich text uses the shared HTMLContent click interceptor to turn same-origin anchors into SPA redirects via CUSTOM_EVENT.REDIRECT/history.push. In the buggy path, that interception treats Ctrl+Click and other modified/non-primary clicks like ordinary left clicks, dispatching an in-tab redirect and preventing the browser's native new-tab behavior even though the anchor itself is valid for the context menu.
approach: Constrain the SPA redirect in HTMLContent to unmodified primary-button clicks on same-origin links that target the current browsing context. Let the browser handle Ctrl+Click, Meta+Click, Shift/Alt modified clicks, middle/right clicks, download links, and non-_self targets by returning before dispatching CUSTOM_EVENT.REDIRECT or calling preventDefault. Keep the change local to the shared renderer so comments, notes, descriptions, and HTML documents inherit the fix.
tests_to_add: HTMLContent dispatches CUSTOM_EVENT.REDIRECT and prevents default for a plain left click on an internal link
HTMLContent does not dispatch redirect or prevent default for Ctrl+Click on an internal link
risk_notes: Some app code may rely on HTMLContent intercepting unusual clicks, but preserving browser defaults for modified/non-primary clicks matches standard anchor behavior.
out_of_scope_observations: The existing link formatter for #content references remains regex-based and is not changed for this issue.
